claims.statement: The Event Dialog allows users to create a new fact and attach a source citation in a single atomic cite_fact operation for both individuals and families.
Surety ratings categorize evidentiary reliability into Direct, Indirect, Negative, and Conflicting levels.
Researchers can select existing source documents or inline-create a new source document directly within the Event Dialog.
Claimed value inputs adapt dynamically based on the selected fact type schema, supporting text, numeric, boolean, enum, and multi-enum values.

Theogony implements an evidence-first architecture where every genealogical fact and event must be tied directly to a source document with a surety rating, page reference, and structured values via atomic operations.
Surety ratings in Theogony categorize evidentiary reliability into Direct, Indirect, Negative, and Conflicting levels to support genealogical analysis under the Genealogical Proof Standard (GPS).

Family structures and relationships, such as parent-child and spouse connections, are established and cited using structured evidence links and status markers (active, disputed, rejected) to prevent data loss from conflicting records.
